title: The Lipid Paradox in Chronic Liver Disease: Integrative Evidence From Intrahepatic Transcriptomics and Population-based Cohorts.
authors: Su S, Chen Z, Ye Y, Yin W, Li F, Liu A
journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Chronic liver disease (CLD) is associated with major metabolic disturbances. Although an elevated atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) reflects cardiometabolic risk, progressive liver dysfunction may instead be accompanied by lipid depletion, suggesting a "lipid paradox." We aimed to investigate its intrahepatic transcriptomic basis, systemic manifestations, and clinical implications using an integrative molecular-to-population approach. METHODS: Intrahepatic transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes associated with chronic hepatitis B progression, and hub genes were screened by machine learning. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2015-2018 data were used to examine the association between the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) and AIP using survey-weighted models and mediation analyses. Data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) were used to model 4-yr AIP trajectories and explore associations with cardiometabolic outcomes and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Transcriptomics identified nine immune-fibrotic hub genes; functional enrichment showed immune activation and matrix remodeling with suppressed lipid metabolism. In NHANES, higher fibrosis risk was independently associated with lower AIP, with mediation more consistent with metabolic depletion than inflammation and independent of the age term in FIB-4. In CHARLS, individuals with liver disease showed an attenuated AIP trajectory; within this subgroup, lower AIP was associated with a higher prevalence of cardiovascular disease and metabolic syndrome, with an exploratory adverse survival signal. CONCLUSION: Across transcriptomic, cross-sectional, and longitudinal analyses, reduced AIP in CLD may reflect metabolic and nutritional vulnerability rather than cardiometabolic protection, warranting further evaluation as an indicator for risk stratification.

title: Advanced cell-instructive bio-inks: Engineering multiscale niches for functional tissue formation.
authors: Ng WL, Xu Y, Liu F, Bartolo P
abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has transformed tissue fabrication by enabling the precise spatial organization of living cells and biomaterials into biomimetic tissue constructs. However, advances in manufacturing have outpaced the development of bio-inks capable of actively directing tissue formation. Most existing bio-inks remain optimized for printability, rheological behaviour, and structural fidelity, while providing limited control over the biological processes that govern tissue morphogenesis, functional maturation, and regeneration. This review examines the emerging paradigm of cell-instructive bio-inks, which integrate biological regulation directly into material design to recreate the cellular microenvironments that guide tissue development. We present a unifying framework that classifies these bio-inks according to three complementary regulatory dimensions: biochemical niches that regulate cell fate through molecular signalling and regenerative matrices; architectural niches that direct tissue organization through spatial and structural cues; and metabolic niches that modulate oxygen availability, redox homeostasis, and cellular metabolism. We further discuss strategies for integrating these instructive functions within multifunctional bio-inks, together with scalable manufacturing, and artificial intelligence-assisted bio-ink design. By redefining bio-inks as active regulators of cellular behaviour, this review establishes a conceptual framework for engineering next-generation bio-inks capable of orchestrating tissue development, functional maturation, and regenerative outcomes.

title: Artificial Intelligence in suicide prevention: promise, peril, and clinical implications for clinical practice.
authors: Nobile B, Courtet P
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into psychiatry is progressing rapidly, with promising yet underexplored applications in suicide prevention. While most existing studies have focused on suicide risk prediction, AI could be applied more broadly across the suicide prevention continuum. This review explores AI's potential in improving the detection of suicidal ideation (SI), enhancing clinician training, and expanding patient access to psychotherapeutic support. Studies suggest that AI models may identify SI more sensitively than clinicians by detecting subtle linguistic or semantic cues. Furthermore, AI-based virtual patients have been shown to improve clinicians' confidence and accuracy in suicide risk assessments, particularly when used alongside traditional training methods. On the patient side, CBT-inspired AI tools offer scalable, on-demand support, but most remain unregulated and clinically unvalidated. Despite their perceived empathy and availability, such tools pose ethical and clinical risks. Many patients use AI tools without professional guidance, a trend clinicians often underestimate. This disconnect calls for urgent regulatory oversight and professional engagement. Without clear clinical validation, AI-based tools may evolve outside medical frameworks, exposing vulnerable individuals to preventable harm. Psychiatry must not only adapt but also lead, ensuring that innovation is harnessed responsibly to serve patients with empathy, safety, and scientific rigor.

title: Breaking the degenerative triad: Microenvironment reprogramming biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration.
authors: Zhao X, Han X, Hu Z, Chen Y, Wang X, Liu Q, Hu X, Zhang Q
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

title: Microenvironmental barriers to healing in osteoradionecrosis and opportunities for regenerative intervention.
authors: La Croix AE, Torres Gouveia ME, Bertone PM, Nemanic NM, Bahney CS, Hixon KR
abstract: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a debilitating sequela of radiotherapy (RT) for head and neck cancer (HNC), characterized by persistent bone exposure or radiographic non-viability and profound tissue repair failure. Despite advances in radiation delivery and clinical management, ORN remains challenging to treat, with therapeutic strategies largely focused on symptom control, infection mitigation, or surgical reconstruction rather than restoration of regenerative capacity. Emerging evidence suggests that radiation-induced cellular senescence represents a central and underrecognized driver of ORN pathophysiology. Ionizing radiation disrupts the bone microenvironment through sustained vascular injury, impaired osteogenic-angiogenic coupling, chronic inflammation, and the accumulation of senescent bone-resident and stromal cells that secrete a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Together, these changes create a hostile niche that suppresses bone remodeling and wound healing long after radiation exposure. This review synthesizes current understanding of radiation-induced injury to the bone microenvironment, critically evaluates existing classification systems and treatment strategies for ORN, and examines emerging regenerative approaches. We further propose senotherapeutic strategies targeting radiation-induced cellular senescence as a complementary and potentially transformative avenue to restore tissue repair capacity. By integrating regenerative biomaterials with targeted modulation of senescence, future therapies may move beyond palliation toward true biological resolution of ORN. Biomaterial delivery systems (e.g., injectable hydrogels, mineral composite scaffolds, and cryogel platforms) are emerging as promising vehicles for spatiotemporally controlled senotherapeutic delivery within the irradiated bone niche.

title: Recent advances in functionalized electrospun nanofibers for biomedical and therapeutic applications: A comprehensive review.
authors: Deshmukh K, Pandey M, Moulahoum H, Ghorbanizamani F, Kovářík T, Przekora-Kuśmierz A, Jena H, Vora M
abstract: Electrospun nanofibers (ESNFs) have become a major focus of modern research given their adaptable architecture, extensive interface, and distinctive physicochemical characteristics, making them appropriate for varied applications such as catalysis and environmental cleanup, drug delivery (DD), tissue engineering (TE), sensing, actuation, and various energy-related technologies. As a result, electrospinning (ES) has emerged as a versatile manufacturing technique, driving intensive efforts to engineer nanofibrous structures specifically for biomedical purposes. Functionalization of ESNFs can be achieved by embedding functional agents or altering surface chemistry to introduce specific functionalities. This review discusses the fabrication methods, optimization techniques, and broad biomedical applications of modified ESNFs, emphasizing their key properties, including biocompatibility, degradability, and safety profile. The article outlines various strategies for creating and modifying ESNFs, followed by a comprehensive analysis of their applications in tissue regeneration, DD, wound repair, antimicrobial therapy, cancer diagnostics and treatment, and biosensing. By critically evaluating recent advances, highlighting future directions, and addressing ongoing challenges about ES, this review underscores the transformative potential of functionalized ESNFs as efficient and adaptable biomaterials for biomedical technologies.

title: A target amplification-free CRISPR biosensor with digital microfluidic processing for microRNA profiling in AI-enhanced pediatric sepsis diagnosis.
authors: Huang D, Shi S, Wang X, Li W, Zhang X, Xiang W, Xu Z, He Y
abstract: MicroRNA signatures provide an informative readout of host-response dysregulation in pediatric sepsis, but their clinical translation remains limited by low target abundance and multiplexing requirements. Here, a target amplification-free CRISPR biosensing platform was established. The sensing mechanism couples Cas13a target recognition to promoter release, template reconstruction, and transcription-driven Cas13a reactivation, enabling fluorescence amplification through internal molecular cycling without amplifying the target miRNAs. Then, an electrowetting-based digital microfluidic chip was designed to compartmentalize parallel reactions and automate droplet generation, reaction assembly, isothermal incubation, magnetic separation, and fluorescence readout. Under optimized conditions, four sepsis-associated biomarkers (miR-15a, miR-21, miR-146a, and miR-155) and the reference control (snRNA U44) were detected at attomolar levels (expected mean input of 1.67 molecules per reaction) with good specificity and minimal inter-droplet interference. The resulting miRNA profiles were then used as input features for machine learning-enhanced sepsis classification and risk assessment. In 252 clinical samples, the resulting model achieved a test-set AUC of 0.973 and an overall accuracy of 92.1%. The model-derived risk score was associated with the Phoenix Sepsis Score and, in a representative longitudinal case, showed preliminary potential to reflect disease evolution. Overall, this platform enables automated analysis of disease-associated miRNA signatures and demonstrates its potential for in-vitro diagnosis of pediatric sepsis.

title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells.
authors: Bayaraa O, Lee NH, Kim SH, Lee H, Li CJ, Fu X, Hyun J, Choi G
abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

title: CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit for highly sensitive detection of aflatoxin B1.
authors: Wu Z, Ma Y, Li X, Yan Z, Huang Y, Wang K, Quan W, Mo L
abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a highly toxic mycotoxin and strongly carcinogenic and teratogenic to humans. Achieving CRISPR-based sensing system for highly sensitive detection of AFB1 remains a significant challenge. A CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit (CPSCN) is proposed for the sensitive and accurate detection of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1). In the CPSCN sensing system, CRISPR/Cas12a/gRNA1 indirectly recognizes AFB1 by aptamer and effectively triggers trans-cleavage of a pair of self-reporting single-stranded DNA-locked RNA2 fluorescence probes (named as dual-winged fluorescence probe). The released RNA2 then initiates an autocatalytic positive feedback loop, resulting in continuous probe cleavage. The CPSCN system achieves highly sensitive detection in a single-enzyme one-step process. The method exhibits excellent quantitative capability for AFB1 detection with a detection limit of 7.5 pg/mL. In real samples, the detection results of the proposed biosensor show high consistency with those obtained by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). This work not only provides a novel strategy for AFB1 detection with high sensitivity, robustness, and operational simplicity, but also offers a new insight for designing signal amplification strategies of CRISPR-based biosensors.

title: DNA assisting CRISPR-Cas13a activation regulating assay for detection of DNA mutation and miRNAs.
authors: Wan C, Liu W, Pan S, Wang X, Zhou J, Hu Y, Li P, Nie X
abstract: Cas13a is an RNA-targeting effector system with exceptional sensitivity, essential for applications such as mutation discrimination, RNA biomarker quantification and dynamic monitoring. However, precise control over its activation kinetics and thermodynamics remains a fundamental challenge, limiting its use in nucleic acid detection. Here, we present the DNA-Assisting CRISPR-Cas13a Activation Regulating (DACAR) Assay, which employs a single-stranded DNA blocker to occupy the crRNA spacer. Through programmable toehold-mediated strand displacement (TMSD) and toehold-exchange (TE) reactions, DACAR is able to control the thermodynamics and kinetics of Cas13a activation at two different levels. Systematic modulation of toehold length and direction yields a tunable cleavage rate gradient, while TE-based free-energy tuning facilitates an ON/OFF gating mode. For single-nucleotide variant (SNV) discrimination, DACAR-TE amplifies thermodynamic mismatch effects, achieving a discrimination factor of 162.4 and a detection limit of 0.05% mutant abundance for the KRAS G12D mutation. The Switch-DACAR system also enables sequential detection of miR-155 and miR-21 in a single tube, with a detection limit of 10 pM. To sum up, DACAR provides a unified, programmable framework for precise molecular-level control of Cas13a, advancing its potential in diagnostics and molecular logic.

title: DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel reprograms the immuno-oxidative microenvironment to support stem cell-based cartilage repair in osteoarthritis.
authors: Yu H, Hu Z, Tan Q, Wang C, Wang B, Yan Y, Yu Y, Zhang F
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease, and stem cell therapy is often limited by a hostile joint microenvironment. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and damage-associated cell-free DNA (cfDNA) cooperatively drive innate immune activation, inflammatory macrophage polarization, and chondrogenic instability, forming an immuno-oxidative barrier to cartilage repair. Here, we developed a bioactive DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel (MNKB/HA) to remodel this niche and enhance BMSC-mediated cartilage repair. MNKB/HA integrates Mn3O4 nanozymes with Kartogenin (KGN)-engineered bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) in an injectable hyaluronic acid matrix. Mn3O4 exhibited SOD- and CAT-like activities, scavenging O2·-, H2O2, and ·OH, while efficiently adsorbing cfDNA and CpG-ODN to suppress TLR9/MyD88 signaling and M1 polarization and promote M2 polarization. In vitro, 10 μg/mL Mn3O4 was cytocompatible, protected BMSCs and chondrocytes from H2O2-induced apoptosis, and reshaped inflammatory secretion, with IL-10 increased 8.3-fold and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β reduced. KGN stabilized the chondrogenic phenotype (SOX9, COL Ⅱ, ACAN), while its combination with Mn3O4 synergistically enhanced chondrogenic stability under oxidative/inflammatory stress. In rat OA, intra-articular MNKB/HA reduced OARSI scores, restored COL II and ACAN, decreased MMP13, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and attenuated synovitis and osteophytes. MNKB/HA also reduced synovial cfDNA, weakened TLR9 signaling, promoted M2 polarization, and showed intra-articular retention for at least 10 days without notable systemic toxicity. Thus, MNKB/HA remodels the immuno-oxidative niche through synergistic ROS scavenging and cfDNA adsorption, providing a strategy for stem cell-mediated cartilage repair in OA.

title: A DNAzyme-activated engineered crRNA enables CRISPR-Cas12a biosensing of ALP and S. aureus.
authors: Wang X, Shi X, Zheng X, Ding Y, Jing Y, Zhang J, Wang J, Li H
abstract: CRISPR-Cas12a biosensing is hindered by insufficient sensitivity that necessitates pre-amplification, as well as the limited ability to directly detect non-nucleic-acid targets. Herein, we developed a CRISPR-Cas12a biosensor centered on a DNAzyme-activated engineered crRNA (e-crRNA), enabling Mn2+-responsive control over its trans-cleavage activity for nucleic-acid-amplification-free detection. Upon Mn2+-dependent activation, the DNAzyme cleaved the e-crRNA to liberate a full-sized crRNA1 and a split crRNA2. The combined crRNA1/crRNA2 system enhanced Cas12a trans-cleavage activity, compensating for the activity loss associated with crRNA engineering. Rational design of the split site further improved the signal-to-noise ratio. Moreover, by gating the system activation on Mn2+, the non-specific activation effects caused by spurious DNA hybridization were mitigated. When coupled with a Mn2+-responsive signal conversion strategy, this platform achieved sensitive detection of alkaline phosphatase with the LOD of 0.008 U/L and Staphylococcus aureus with the LOD of 29.76 CFU/mL. This study showcased the innovative use of Mn2+-dependent DNAzyme to efficiently activate CRISPR-Cas12a system, establishing a powerful platform for biosensing.

title: Target-triggered exponential amplification-enhanced CRISPR/Cas12a system with a fluorescence-quenching lateral flow assay for ultrasensitive detection of Salmonella typhimurium.
authors: Xiong Y, Li L, Huang J, Shen XA, Sun J, Guo Y, Liu D, Ma T
abstract: The use of the CRISPR/Cas12a system combined with lateral flow assays shows significant promise for point-of-care testing in resource-limited regions. However, the use of isothermal amplification technologies to preenrich target DNA fragments inherently increases the risk of aerosol contamination during strip testing. Here, we introduce a target-triggered exponential amplification-enhanced CRISPR/Cas12a system combined with a fluorescence-quenching lateral flow assay (TEA-FQLFA) for ultrasensitive detection of Salmonella typhimurium. The TEA system converts a single Cas12a recognition event into sequential dual Cas12a activation, initiating a cleavage cascade amplification that achieves a 106-fold signal enhancement without the need for a target DNA preamplification operation. Moreover, hyperbranched gold-coated polymer microspheres (HGPMs), characterized by ultrahigh extinction coefficients and a broad absorption band in the 300-800 nm range, are utilized as fluorescence quenching reporters of the FQLFA for simultaneous colorimetric visualization and fluorescence-based quantitative detection of target DNA concentration. By leveraging the synergistic integration of TEA-mediated signal amplification and HGPM-enabled optical signal enhancement, the TEA-FQLFA system achieves attomolar-level detection of target DNA (0.081 aM) and enables sensitive detection of Salmonella typhimurium in complex food matrices, with detection limits of 7.95 CFU/mL in colorimetric mode and 6.94 CFU/mL in fluorescence mode. In summary, this work establishes a versatile platform that integrates cascade signal amplification with dual-mode lateral-flow for ultrasensitive food safety detection.

title: Unipoint-anchored cascade amplification strategy integrating FUSE probe-activated CRISPR-Cas12a for dual mode osteopontin detection toward osteosarcoma assessment and therapeutic response evaluation.
authors: Zhao J, Gao M, Ding H, Song Y, Zhang Y, Ten Y, Wang F, Miao Z
abstract: Reliable assessment of disease status and therapeutic response in osteosarcoma remains an unmet clinical need. Integrative bioinformatics analysis and protein-level verification in paired clinical specimens prioritized secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1, osteopontin) as a liquid biopsy target associated with osteosarcoma progression and patient survival. On this basis, CRUMP, a CRISPR-Cas12a and FUSE Probe-based dual-mode biosensing platform, was developed for SPP1 quantification. A bifunctional NH2-ZIF-8 probe co-immobilizes the components required for target recognition and Cas12a activation, while MoS2@AuNPs interfaces transduce the resulting signals. Signal amplification is achieved through a unipoint-anchored multisite cascade based on a DNA tetrahedron-HCR architecture, enabling one-to-multiple parallel amplification while balancing stability and sensitivity. A single Cas12a cleavage event simultaneously decreases the electrochemical (EC) signal and increases the fluorescence (FL) signal. These reciprocal changes allow the two readouts to provide an internal consistency check for each measurement. Each channel covers more than five orders of magnitude, with detection limits of 167.7 fg/mL for EC and 331.6 fg/mL for FL. The broad measurement ranges allow most serum samples to be analyzed directly, without the per-sample dilution optimization that ELISA requires, and the complete analysis takes only approximately 85 min. Validation across osteosarcoma cell lines, clinical specimens, and tumor-bearing mouse models provided preliminary evidence for the feasibility of CRUMP in SPP1 quantification and endpoint assessment of chemotherapeutic response. By combining biomarker prioritization, biosensor engineering, and preliminary application testing, this work presents CRUMP as a candidate platform for SPP1-based assessment of osteosarcoma and its therapeutic response.

title: SF2O-SKDCN: Selective kernel attention enabled deep learning framework for cardiovascular disease detection using photoplethysmography signals.
authors: Chavan PM, Joshi KR, Kamathe RS
abstract: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) is a lethal disease that needs early intervention to prevent further harm and eventually safeguard patients' lives. Therefore, CVD detection is critical for effective disease management. Even though practical findings are made using traditional detection methods, they mostly struggle with overfitting risks, generalizability issues, and computational overhead challenges during the detection process. Therefore, the research proposes Sail Tuna Fish Foraging Optimized-Selective Kernel attention-enabled Deep Convolutional Neural Network (SF2O-SKDCN) that utilizes photoplethysmography (PPG) signals, which are extensively used in clinical applications as a screening tool, and the heart rate feature descriptor is introduced to extract the crucial feature from the segmented signal. Further, the Selective Kernel Shuffle (SKS) attention enables the model to focus only on the predominant CVD features, thereby enhancing the interpretability characteristics. In addition, actively tuning the model hyperparameters using the Sail Tuna Fish Foraging Optimization (SF2O) algorithm prevents local convergence and vanishing gradient issues. Experimenting with the MIMIC II dataset, the model yields better results by achieving 98.54% accuracy, 99.07% recall, 98.05% Positive predictive value, and 99.05% Negative predictive value for 90% training.

title: Site-regulated CoNFs-NH2@PtNPs nanozyme-based all-in-one portable detection of organophosphorus pesticides integrating deep learning and hardware logic gates.
authors: Zhang Y, Gao D, He P, Peng H, Xu P, Qiu P
abstract: Widespread use of organophosphorus pesticides (OPs) has led to pervasive environmental residues and potential human health hazards, making rapid, sensitive, and portable on-site OPs detection urgently needed. In this work, an amino-functionalized cobalt nanoflower-supported platinum nanoparticle composite (CoNFs-NH2@PtNPs) was successfully fabricated. Combined with steady-state kinetic experiments and density functional theory calculations, the modulation mechanism of amino modification on the electron-donating ability of Pt active sites and oxygen activation performance was systematically clarified. Taking advantage of the inherent oxidase-like activity and fluorescence properties of CoNFs-NH2@PtNPs, a colorimetric-fluorescent dual-mode sensor was constructed based on acetylcholinesterase inhibition for high-efficiency OPs detection. Furthermore, a low-cost integrated portable detection platform was developed by integrating 3D-printed dark-box hardware, MCU control modules, smartphone imaging technology, and self-built sensing algorithms. This platform realizes intuitive qualitative grading via LED indicator lights based on solution RGB signal changes and intelligent quantitative detection through a customized smartphone mini-program. The established all-in-one detection system effectively addresses the poor portability and inferior real-time performance of traditional OPs detection methods, providing a reliable and practical strategy for field pesticide residue monitoring.

Spatial organization of magnetic nanoparticles in chitosan-gelatin hydrogels enables enhanced magnetic actuation and cell response under dynamic stimulation.
authors: Viteri A, Ginebra MP, García-Torres J
abstract: Magnetically responsive hydrogels have emerged as promising platforms for remotely modulating HFF-1 fibroblasts behavior through dynamic mechanical stimulation; however, the influence of magnetic nanoparticle spatial organization on magnetic actuation and cell response remains unexplored. Herein, we report the development of chitosan-gelatin magnetic hydrogels with controlled Fe3O4 nanoparticle distribution including homogeneously dispersed, and spatially patterned configurations, as a strategy to engineer localized mechanotransduction and magnetic actuation. The role of nanoparticle organization on the physicochemical, magnetic, and biological properties of the hydrogels has been analyzed. Structural characterization confirmed the successful incorporation of Fe3O4 nanoparticles while preserving their crystalline inverse spinel structure. Morphological and topographical analyses revealed that patterned hydrogels exhibit well-defined nanoparticle-rich and nanoparticle-free regions, generating pronounced microscale heterogeneity throughout the material. The incorporation and spatial confinement of Fe3O4 nanoparticles significantly influenced the hydrogel properties, increasing stiffness, reducing swelling capacity, and enhancing magnetic responsiveness. Notably, patterned hydrogels displayed higher saturation magnetization and magnetic susceptibility than homogeneously dispersed systems, indicating that nanoparticle confinement promotes cooperative magnetic interactions and more efficient magnetic actuation. Biological studies demonstrated excellent cytocompatibility for all hydrogel formulations. While static magnetic stimulation slightly reduced fibroblast proliferation, dynamic magnetic stimulation significantly enhanced cell proliferation, spreading, and cytoskeletal organization, particularly in patterned hydrogels. These effects are attributed to cyclic mechanical cues generated by amplified magnetic-to-mechanical transduction within the patterned magnetic domains. Overall, this study demonstrates that nanoparticle spatial organization is a key design parameter for engineering magnetically responsive hydrogels with tunable magnetic actuation and controllable cellular responses for tissue engineering applications.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Three-dimensional and dynamic assessment of digital lymphatic vessels using photoacoustic imaging.
authors: Suzuki Y, Uno T, Kajita H, Kato T, Takatsume Y, Imanishi N, Kishi K
abstract: Digital lymphatic anatomy has been defined largely by cadaveric studies. We evaluated whether photoacoustic lymphangiography (PAL) could depict three-dimensional anatomy and motion-related deformation in vivo. Two healthy volunteers and one patient with secondary upper-extremity lymphedema underwent fingertip indocyanine green injection, near-infrared fluorescence imaging, and static and dynamic PAL. In healthy fingers, lymphatic vessels coursed mainly along the lateral aspects toward the dorsal hand and lay between superficial veins and digital arteries. Flexion produced spiral-like deformation or abrupt angulation, whereas vessels were relatively straight during extension; segmental lymphatic signals moved proximally during motion. In the patient, PAL visualized vessels beneath dermal backflow that appeared more irregular and showed frequent short-segment tortuosity, and guided lymphaticovenular anastomosis. These findings support the feasibility of finger-specific, in vivo three-dimensional and motion-resolved assessment of digital lymphatic morphology using PAL.

title: Feasibility and potential benefits of daily online adaptive radiotherapy for head and neck cancer without margin reduction using an RTT-only workflow.
authors: Lindegaard AM, Håkansson K, Appelt A, Bernsdorf M, Gothelf AB, Jensen TRB, Mohammad A, Kristensen CA
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Online adaptive radiotherapy (oART) may improve head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment, where anatomical changes during radiotherapy (RT) are common. However, oART is resource-intensive and clinical data are limited. We conducted a prospective feasibility trial implementating an RT technologist (RTT)-led workflow to evaluate dosimetric outcomes, workflow strategies, and intrafractional motion in daily oART. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Ten patients receiving curatively intended oART (33-34 fractions) using standard PTV margins were included (NCT: 07506902). For each fraction, a scheduled plan (original plan recalculated on daily anatomy) and an adapted plan (reoptimized to daily anatomy) were generated, and the preferred plan was delivered. Target coverage (PTV1 V95%), mean dose (Dmean) and maximum dose (Dmax) to selected organs at risk (OAR), treatment time, and baseline target volume were extracted for all fractions. The effect of oART (scheduled- versus delivered plan) was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Intrafractional motion was assessed weekly. RESULTS: A total of 322 adaptive session were completed. The median treatment time was 29.9 min. The adapted plan was selected in 78% of fractions. oART improved target coverage in 76% of fractions. Dmean decreased for the oral cavity (-2.4 Gy, p < 0.001) but increased for the middle PCM (2.5 Gy, p < 0.001). Dmax increased for the brainstem (2.9 Gy, p < 0.001) and spinal cord (2.2 Gy, p < 0.001). Intrafractional motion was within PTV margins, with few patient-specific exceedances. CONCLUSION: Daily oART for HNC is feasible with improvements in target coverage but modest and inconsistent OAR sparing.

title: Effects of sitagliptin combined with GTS-21 on improving glycemic control and diabetic nephropathy by anti-apoptosis in Leprdb/db mice.
authors: Tian W, Wang W, Tang S, Su L, Cooney R, Tian X, Meng Q
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Activation of α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7nAChR) by GTS-21 engages the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway (CAP). This study investigated adding GTS-21 to sitagliptin, a DPP-4 inhibitor used to increase endogenous GLP-1, confers additional benefit over sitagliptin monotherapy on glycemic control and diabetic nephropathy (DN) in Leprdb/db mice, focusing on anti-apoptotic mechanisms. METHODS: Leptin receptor-deficient (Leprdb/db, 8-week-old) mice were randomized into control (saline), sitagliptin (20 mg/kg), or combination (sitagliptin 20 mg/kg + GTS-21 4 mg/kg) groups for 4 weeks. Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), serum creatinine (Scr), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and IL-6 were measured. Renal histology was evaluated by H&E staining. Apoptosis was assessed by TUNEL staining and cleaved caspase-3 expression. In vitro, HK-2 cells exposed to high glucose (30 mM) were treated with liraglutide (100 nM) and/or GTS-21 (20 nM) to examine apoptosis. RESULTS: Combination therapy significantly improved glucose tolerance at weeks 1 and 4 (AUC reduction, P = 0.0366 and P = 0.0435 vs control), whereas sitagliptin alone showed no effect. Both treatments reduced Scr (P = 0.0002 for combination; P = 0.0101 for monotherapy), but only combination therapy attenuated renal histological injury (P = 0.002) and decreased IL-6 in serum and kidney (P = 0.0433 and P = 0.0041). Renal apoptosis was also suppressed, with reduced TUNEL-positive cells (P = 0.0043) and cleaved caspase-3 (P = 0.0122). In HK-2 cells, high glucose increased cleaved caspase-3 (P = 0.0324), which was attenuated by liraglutide plus GTS-21 (P = 0.0320). CONCLUSIONS: Add-on GTS-21 to sitagliptin improved glycemic control and attenuated diabetic nephropathy beyond sitagliptin monotherapy in Leprdb/db mice, with reduced renal inflammation and suppressed apoptosis. These findings suggest that combined activation of GLP-1 receptor and α7nAChR signaling warrants further investigation as a renoprotective strategy in diabetic nephropathy.

title: Tirzepatide alleviates hepatic steatosis and inflammation in MASLD partly through suppression of macrophage Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB signaling.
authors: He Y, Ma T, Xing H, Cao X, Song F, Pan Y, Ren L
abstract: Metabolic stress, hepatic lipid accumulation, and macrophage-associated sterile inflammation are closely involved in the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Tirzepatide improves metabolic outcomes, but its effects on macrophage inflammatory signaling in MASLD remain unclear. This study investigated the protective effects of tirzepatide against high-fat, high-fructose diet (HFHFD)-induced MASLD and examined the potential involvement of macrophage Dectin-1/spleen tyrosine kinase (Syk)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling. After 7 weeks of HFHFD feeding to establish the MASLD model, male C57BL/6J mice received tirzepatide (10 nmol/kg, subcutaneously, every 3 days) for an additional 7 weeks. Biochemical assays, histology, hepatic RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence were performed. Palmitic acid (PA)-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, siRNA-mediated Dectin-1 knockdown, and a RAW264.7 cell-derived conditioned medium-based macrophage-hepatocyte indirect interaction model were used for mechanistic validation. Tirzepatide treatment improved HFHFD-induced metabolic dysfunction, liver injury, hepatic steatosis, and inflammatory responses in mice. RNA-seq revealed enrichment of C-type lectin receptor and NF-κB signaling pathways, while HFHFD-induced Clec7a upregulation was reversed by tirzepatide. Tirzepatide reduced hepatic macrophage accumulation, Dectin-1 expression, and Syk/p65 phosphorylation. In PA-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, tirzepatide suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and secretion and inhibited Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB activation. Conditioned medium from tirzepatide-treated RAW264.7 cells attenuated lipid accumulation and abnormalities in lipid metabolism- and inflammation-related gene expression in HepG2 cells. Dectin-1 knockdown itself attenuated PA-induced inflammatory responses and was associated with a reduced additional response to tirzepatide. These findings suggest that tirzepatide alleviates HFHFD-induced MASLD, with suppression of macrophage Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB signaling potentially contributing to these effects.

title: Disseminated CNS tuberculosis in SLE without anti-TNF exposure: implications for LTBI screening in endemic settings-case report.
authors: Kamadi E, Hawken M, Shah R, Otieno F
abstract: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are vulnerable to tuberculosis (TB) because of disease-related immune dysfunction, immunosuppressive therapy, and background exposure in TB-endemic settings. Although latent TB infection (LTBI) screening is routinely recommended before biologic and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), guidance for glucocorticoids, conventional DMARDs, and other immunosuppressive therapies is less prescriptive. We report 2 HIV-negative Kenyan women with established SLE who developed disseminated extrapulmonary TB after approximately 12 and 20 months of mycophenolate mofetil therapy, respectively, while also receiving maintenance prednisolone 10 mg daily. The second patient had also received rituximab 7 months before TB diagnosis. In case 1, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) GeneXpert Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB)/rifampicin and gluteal-abscess culture-confirmed disseminated central nervous system (CNS) TB with bilateral gluteal involvement. In case 2, lymph-node histology and culture-confirmed TB in the setting of widespread lymphadenopathy and splenic microabscesses; despite negative CSF investigations, neuroimaging demonstrated a cerebral lesion radiologically consistent with tuberculoma. Both patients received anti-TB therapy with adjunctive corticosteroids for CNS disease. Both patients demonstrated eventual clinical and radiological improvement. These cases demonstrate that severe disseminated TB, including CNS involvement, may occur in patients with SLE receiving nontumour necrosis factor (TNF) immunosuppressive regimens in TB-endemic settings. Although causal effects of individual immunosuppressive agents cannot be established, the cases support structured TB-risk assessment and a low threshold for LTBI testing before prolonged corticosteroid exposure or combination immunosuppression. Risk-stratified national guidance specifying therapy-related triggers for LTBI assessment may improve implementation and reduce preventable TB morbidity in high-burden settings.

title: Trait-like proteomic signatures of stress resilience: correlates of freeze-like response resistance.
authors: Kučera J, Makarová M, Vít M, Novák J, Zlámal F, Ráčková L, Fialová Kučerová J, Grulichová M
abstract: The freeze-like response is a fundamental defensive mechanism that remains poorly understood despite its potential to impair functioning under acute threat. We examined its biological correlates using untargeted serum proteomics in participants exposed to ecologically valid simulated armed attacks, comparing untrained individuals (n = 20) with experienced police rapid response personnel (n = 20). Freeze-like responses, characterized by unresponsiveness to attack, were assessed via expert video analysis of participant performance during the scenarios. Serum samples collected before and after threat exposure were analyzed via LC‒MS/MS, identifying 1,238 protein groups. Experienced personnel demonstrated markedly greater resistance to freeze-like responses. No significant proteomic changes were observed from pre- to post-exposure in either group, suggesting that freeze-resistance may be associated with stable, trait-like signatures rather than acute stress-responsive processes. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified a module strongly correlated with freeze-resistance (r = 0.75, p = 4 × 10-9) and training status (r = 0.71, p = 6 × 10-8), which also correlated with skeletal muscle mass (r = 0.57, p = 8 × 10-5). This module was enriched for processes including extracellular matrix organization, muscle development, carbohydrate metabolism, and antioxidant activity. These molecular patterns may reflect the downstream effects of comprehensive training that integrates physical conditioning, operational experience, and psychological preparation. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of freeze-like response resistance under realistic threat conditions, supporting the view that resilience involves stable physiological adaptations rather than solely reactive stress mechanisms.

title: Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism.
authors: Ahamba IS, Song G, Kinkpe L, Duan Q, Goswami N, Jin Z, Wu J, Dong X
abstract: Intramuscular fat (IMF) significantly influences meat quality, affecting flavor, tenderness, and juiciness. Despite extensive research on livestock such as cattle and pigs, the regulation of IMF in rabbits remains poorly understood. This study establishes a standardized in vitro method for isolating and characterizing intramuscular preadipocytes from the longissimus dorsi muscle of 3-day-old Hycole rabbits using enzymatic digestion and differential centrifugation. Three-day-old neonates were selected for initial protocol development due to their higher progenitor cell abundance and tissue accessibility, which facilitates method optimization and ensures consistent cell yields. Isolated cells displayed typical preadipocyte morphology and expressed key markers, including PREF-1, PPARγ, and Leptin, confirmed by RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence. Upon adipogenic induction, cells exhibited progressive lipid accumulation, as indicated by Oil Red O staining, and showed upregulated expression of PPARG, C/EBPa, and FABP4, confirming their differentiation potential. This study establishes a comprehensive protocol for isolating rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes, providing a foundational tool for investigating the molecular mechanisms of adipogenesis in lagomorphs. The model supports future studies on genetic and nutritional strategies to enhance rabbit meat quality while preserving its lean characteristics.

title: Prototype-Guided Test-Time Adaptation for Real-Time EMG-Based Gesture Recognition.
authors: Ma Y, Wang Y, Dai C, Guo Y
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) signals facilitate intuitive human-machine interaction and are widely employed in applications such as prosthetics and rehabilitation. However, sEMG signal distributions are highly sensitive to variations in electrode placement, user physiology, and session conditions, which significantly hinder model generalization in real-world settings. To address this, we propose EMG-based structure-aware test-time adaptive refinement (EMG-STAR), a test-time adaptation (TTA) framework tailored for online deployment without access to target data during training. EMG-STAR improves model stability by fusing historical and batch-wise normalization statistics from both source and target domains, effectively alleviating domain shifts. Furthermore, it refines predictions using a prototype-assisted feature clustering method that enforces consistency among semantically similar target samples. To further enhance reliability, the framework jointly leverages prediction confidence and distributional alignment to filter out noisy pseudo-labels during adaptation. Comprehensive evaluations conducted on two public datasets, Hyser, and NinaPro-DB2, demonstrate that EMG-STAR consistently outperforms ten existing TTA methods. Interpretability analysis using Grad-CAM reveals that EMG-STAR predominantly attends to physiologically meaningful muscle activation regions, suggesting that the model captures neuromuscular structures rather than transient signal noise.

title: Coacervate protocells-mediated mitochondrial transplantation restores gut epithelial energetic homeostasis in ulcerative colitis.
authors: Ding B, Chen Y, Jia Y, Li J, Tan Z, Wu W, Ouyang S, Tong B
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is closely linked to mitochondrial dysfunction in intestinal epithelial cells, yet current therapies fail to correct underlying energy metabolism defects. While exogenous mitochondrial transplantation offers a promising strategy, its clinical translation is hindered by rapid loss of mitochondrial bioactivity ex vivo, poor delivery efficiency, and lysosomal degradation following cellular uptake. Here, we developed a biomimetic coacervate-based protocell system (HTP) via liquid-liquid phase separation of polyethylene glycol, tannic acid, and sodium hyaluronate for efficient encapsulation and delivery of functional mitochondria (HTP@Mito). HTP protocells preserved mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP synthesis capacity for up to 72 h in HBSS buffer at 37°C, far exceeding the viability of free mitochondria. Notably, HTP markedly enhanced intracellular delivery of isolated mitochondria via lipid-raft-mediated endocytosis. In a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced murine UC model, rectally administrating HTP@Mito achieved superior therapeutic efficacy via restoring ATP levels and mitochondrial membrane potential, scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS). Furthermore, by reducing oxidative stress, HTP@Mito rescued lysosomal function and restored impaired autophagic flux, thereby promoting mitophagy to clear damaged mitochondria. HTP@Mito treatment also repaired intestinal epithelial tight junctions, restored goblet cell-derived mucus secretion, and rebalanced gut microbiota by increasing beneficial Lachnospiraceae while reducing pathogenic Escherichia-Shigella. Collectively, this work established a versatile, biomimetic organelle delivery platform that could correct mitochondrial energy deficiency in the intestinal epithelium, providing a framework for mitochondrial transplantation in ulcerative colitis.

title: Heterojunction nanozyme achieve highly efficient antibacterial by cuproptosis-like death and ferroptosis-like death.
authors: Wang W, Zhu R, Gui H, Jin X, Wei X, Wang X
abstract: Metal-ion-mediated lethal pathways offers a highly potent strategy for antibacterial treatments. However, relying on single-pathway mechanisms often fails to overwhelm bacterial antioxidant defenses, reducing antibacterial efficacy. This study designed a heterojunction nanozyme (Cu2O/Fe2O3) that induces ferroptosis-like death and copper-mediated metabolic toxicity exhibiting cuproptosis-like features, achieving highly effective antibacterial treatment. Computational chemistry analysis indicates that the Cu2O/Fe2O3 heterointerface establishes a built-in electric field through spontaneous interfacial electron transfer, thereby enhancing its peroxidase (POD)-like activity. Within the acidic bacterial microenvironment, Cu2O/Fe2O3 catalyzes the generation of large amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and releases metal ions, inducing and amplifying ferroptosis-like death, which disrupts the function of ETC enzymes by attacking iron-sulfur clusters. Concurrently, copper ions disrupt the redox balance by depleting bacillithiol (BSH), indirectly increasing bacterial susceptibility and promoting ferroptosis-like death. Furthermore, the accumulation of copper ions triggers severe metabolic impairments that biochemically resemble the cuproptosis cascade, which disrupts key enzymes of the TCA cycle and impairs the synthesis of electron donors (NADH and FADH2), thereby cutting off the supply of substrates to ETC at the upstream stage. Overall, this study demonstrates that triggering bimetallic ion-mediated metabolic disruptions induces an energy crisis in bacteria, providing a reference for multimodal antibacterial strategies.

title: Oxygen-vacancy-rich LDH sonosensitizers potentiate narrow-spectrum antibiotics via membrane-disruption strategy for mixed bacterial wound infections.
authors: Xi L, Liu X, Yu C, Wang T, Liao J, Lv Y, Zhang M, Zhang Y
abstract: Mixed bacterial infections, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens, remain a major global health concern. Achieving efficient treatment of synergistic polymicrobial infections stills a tremendous clinical challenge due to antibiotic permeability barriers and resistance. Here, we construct a defect-engineered layered double hydroxide (LDH)-based sonosensitizer platform loaded with clindamycin (a-CoW/CLD) for mixed bacterial infection therapy, which not only demonstrates high efficacy against Gram-positive bacteria, but also exploits reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated membrane disruption of Gram-negative bacteria to facilitate CLD penetration, thereby achieving broad-spectrum and highly efficient killing of mixed bacteria. The amorphous a-CoW nanosheets, enriched with oxygen vacancies via acid etching, exhibit a substantially narrowed bandgap (1.22 eV) and markedly enhanced charge separation, producing 22.1-fold higher singlet oxygen under ultrasound (US) irradiation compared with pristine CoW. This ROS burst synergized with CLD achieves potent killing of Staphylococcus aureus (>99.9% at 20 μg mL-1). More critically, ROS disrupt the outer membrane of Gram-negative Escherichia coli, promoting CLD internalization and consequently boosting its lethality by 18.4-fold (from ∼5% to >92.1%). Mechanistic transcriptomics reveals ROS and CLD synergy: ROS disrupt the bacterial membrane via lipid peroxidation, enabling CLD penetration to block protein synthesis and metabolism, while ROS also induce oxidative stress, collectively leading to bacterial death. In a murine wound model co-infected with both pathogens, a-CoW/CLD plus US eradicates >99.9% of mixed bacteria, suppresses systemic inflammation, and significantly accelerates angiogenesis and re-epithelialization. This paradigm establishes a low-dose, broad-spectrum sonodynamic-antibiotic strategy that overcomes antibiotic permeability bottleneck, offering a promising therapeutic avenue against mixed bacterial infections.
